> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TM)$ be smooth, and fix constants
$c,\mu_0>0$. Assume
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, equivalently
$d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. A finite smooth singular $k$-chain means
a finite formal real linear combination of smooth singular $k$-simplices,
with the boundary operation of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]].

For a finite smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$, define its charge by

$$Q(\Sigma):=\frac1c\int_\Sigma\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then:

**(a) Gauss charge formula.** For every such $\Sigma$,

$$Q(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_{\partial\Sigma}\star_gF.$$

Consequently, if $\partial\Sigma=0$, then $Q(\Sigma)=0$. This is the
compact-cycle neutrality constraint for a smooth everywhere-defined sourced
field.

**(b) Bounding-surface restriction.** For every finite smooth singular
three-chain $V$, the magnetic flux through its boundary vanishes:

$$\int_{\partial V}F=0.$$

The equation $dF=0$ does not imply that the flux through every closed
two-cycle is zero; this item gives a zero-flux conclusion only when the cycle
is the boundary of a finite smooth chain in the field domain. Likewise, the
electric flux formula in (a) identifies charge with flux only for a bounding
surface.

**(c) Charge balance.** If a finite smooth singular four-chain $C$ satisfies
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for three-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$Q(\Sigma_2)-Q(\Sigma_1)=-Q(B).$$

Equal charge on the two slices therefore requires zero net side flux. No
asymptotic charge or flux at infinity is asserted; noncompact limits require
separate convergence and boundary-flux hypotheses.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose geodesics
and exponential map are those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Point-normal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there is a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ such that, in the components of this chart,

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0,\qquad \partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}.$$

The construction starts from any chart around $p$ and is finite: no frame field
on $U$ and no global trivialization of $TM$ is used.

**(b) Exponential charts.** For every $p\in M$ and every $g_p$-orthonormal
basis $e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$ there is a star-shaped open neighborhood
$W\subseteq T_pM$ of $0$ on which $\exp_p$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open
$U_p\ni p$, and the chart

$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U_p\longrightarrow\mathbb R^4,$$

where $\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ is the coordinate isomorphism of the basis,
satisfies $u(p)=0$ and the same three normal-form identities at $p$ as in (a).
Moreover every geodesic through $p$ has, in the chart $u$, the form
$u(\gamma(t))=(t-t_0)\,k$ for a constant $k\in\mathbb R^4$ whenever
$\gamma(t_0)=p$, $k=\psi(\gamma'(t_0))$, and
$(t-t_0)\gamma'(t_0)\in W$. Thus the portion represented by its radial initial
vector in $W$ is a straight coordinate ray through the origin. This claim is
not made for a later portion of a geodesic that may return to $U_p$ after its
radial initial vector has left $W$. No assertion is made about the second
derivatives of the metric at $p$: the construction is first order and does not
make a neighborhood of $p$ isometric to Minkowski space.

Every symmetric bilinear form on a finite-dimensional real vector space is congruent to exactly one normal form

$$\operatorname{diag}(I_p,-I_q,0_r),\qquad p+q+r=\dim V.$$

Equivalently, the numbers of positive, negative, and zero diagonal entries are independent of the diagonalizing basis.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

derivations.claim:
By [A1], $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The sign identity in
[F1] gives $d*F=\mu_0i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$. Apply $d$ and use $d^2=0$ to get
$d(i_j\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$ since $\mu_0>0$. By the proved density-divergence
identity [F5], this is $(\nabla_aj^a)\mathrm{vol}_g=0$. The volume form is
nowhere zero, so $\nabla_aj^a=0$.

At $p$, put $W=n(p)^\perp$. Every $v\in T_pM$ has the orthogonal
decomposition $v=-g_p(v,n(p))n(p)+(v+g_p(v,n(p))n(p))$; the second term is
orthogonal to $n(p)$. The summands intersect only in zero because
$g_p(n(p),n(p))=-1$, so $T_pM=\mathbb R n(p)\oplus W$ and $\dim W=3$. The
restriction of $g_p$ to $W$ is nondegenerate: a vector in its radical is
orthogonal to both $W$ and $n(p)$, hence to all of $T_pM$, and must be zero.
The first summand has inertia $(0,1,0)$, while $g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$;
[F4] therefore gives inertia $(3,0,0)$ on $W$, so $g_p|_W$ is positive
definite. Choose a basis $w_1,w_2,w_3$ of $W$ and set
$e_1=w_1/\sqrt{g_p(w_1,w_1)}$. Set
$v_2=w_2-g_p(w_2,e_1)e_1$; linear independence gives $v_2\ne0$, and direct
substitution gives $g_p(v_2,e_1)=0$. Set $e_2=v_2/\sqrt{g_p(v_2,v_2)}$.
Next set $v_3=w_3-g_p(w_3,e_1)e_1-g_p(w_3,e_2)e_2$. Independence gives
$v_3\ne0$, and $g_p(v_3,e_1)=g_p(v_3,e_2)=0$ by orthonormality of $e_1,e_2$.
Positive definiteness makes all three denominators positive; set
$e_3=v_3/\sqrt{g_p(v_3,v_3)}$. If needed, reverse $e_3$ so
$(n(p),e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is positively oriented. This is a $g_p$-orthonormal
basis. By [F3], its exponential chart is point-normal and has time axis
$n(p)$; restrict the chart to its intersection with the open domain
$\mathcal D$. Use its component functions
$\widehat E_i=-cF_{0i}$ and
$\widehat B_i=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$. The spatial
coefficient $(dF)_{123}=0$ is
$\partial_1\widehat B_1+\partial_2\widehat B_2+\partial_3\widehat B_3=0$. For each cyclic triple
$(i,j,k)$, $(dF)_{0ij}=0$ reads
$c^{-1}\partial_t\widehat B_k+c^{-1}(\nabla\times\widehat{\mathbf E})_k=0$, hence
$\partial_t\widehat{\mathbf B}+\nabla\times\widehat{\mathbf E}=0$.

The remaining four coefficients of $d*F=\mu_0i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ are
$(d*F)_{123}=c^{-1}
abla\cdot\widehat{\mathbf E}=\mu_0cho$ and
$(d*F)_{0ij}=\varepsilon_{ijk} igl(c^{-2}\partial_t\widehat E_k-(
abla	imes\widehat{\mathbf B})_k igr)=-\mu_0\varepsilon_{ijk}J^k$. Multiplying by $c$ in the first identity and using $\epsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0c^2$ gives $
abla\cdot\widehat{\mathbf E}=ho/\epsilon_0$; the second gives $
abla	imes\widehat{\mathbf B}-c^{-2}\partial_t\widehat{\mathbf E}=\mu_0\mathbf J$. These equations are pointwise in the chosen normal chart; in an inertial Minkowski chart with constant observer $n=\partial_0$ the same component identities hold throughout that chart.

For a finite smooth spacelike chain $\Sigma$, [F2] applies to the sourced equation from step 1.1 and states
$Q(\Sigma)=c^{-1}\int_\Sigma i_j\mathrm{vol}_g=(\mu_0c)^{-1}\int_{\partial\Sigma}*F$. The coefficient and orientation are those fixed in [A1] and [F1]; no limiting surface is used.

Statement case: When j=0, the sourced form equation is source-free and the current-conservation conclusion is 0=0; the homogeneous equations remain part of the claim.
Statement case: A single finite smooth simplex is included; no multiple-component or asymptotic boundary is required.
Nonsmooth fields and singular or distributional sources are explicitly excluded; the point-normal chart is nondegenerate Lorentzian by definition.
Statement case: Only finite chains are integrated; no endpoint at infinity or limiting flux is used.

Statement case: The planned mathematical supplier closure carries AC_ω for the inherited countable tangent/tensor subatlas construction, recorded explicitly as A2. The finite component algebra and finite-chain Stokes calculation use no stronger choice principle.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TM)$ be smooth, and fix constants
$c,\mu_0>0$. Assume

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and no boundary. Write $\Omega^k(M)$ for the smooth real sections of $\Lambda^kT^*M$. The classical electromagnetic field type is a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$. In length-coordinate charts its components have SI unit tesla; its integral over an oriented smooth two-surface has unit weber. The exterior derivative is denoted $d$. A field is **closed** when $dF=0$. Closedness is a field condition, not the same condition as having a global potential.

For an open set $U\subseteq M$, a **local potential** for $F$ on $U$ is a smooth real one-form $A_U\in\Omega^1(U)$ satisfying $dA_U=F|_U$. It is a **global potential** when $U=M$. In a length-coordinate chart the components of $A_U$ have unit tesla metre. This classical real-field description chooses $F$ itself and requires no bundle or global $A$.

An **optional circle-normalized connection sector** adds the mathematical data of a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a connection, using the local-potential and circle-data conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Here $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. Concretely, supply a countable open cover $\{U_i\}$ and smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$ satisfying $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$. On overlap pieces with smooth real lifts $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$, the normalized local connection one-forms $a_i$ satisfy $a_j=a_i+df_{ij}$; in local fibre angles the convention is $\theta_j=\theta_i-f_{ij}$, so $d\theta_i+a_i$ patches. The local curvature forms $da_i$ agree. Fix an independent constant $\kappa_0>0$ with unit weber, and set $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ and $F|_{U_i}=\kappa_0da_i$. Thus $a_i$ has component unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in length coordinates, while $A_i$ has component unit tesla metre. Choosing $P$ and $\kappa_0$ is extra model data; no claim is made that every smooth closed real $F$ is the curvature of such a fixed-normalization connection.

The selected **topological sector** is the fixed pair consisting of the bundle $P$ and the normalization $\kappa_0$; its connection is data on that fixed bundle. Changing $P$ or $\kappa_0$ selects a different sector.

In a trivialization, a **gauge transformation** is a single-valued smooth map $h:U\to U(1)$; its local real lifts may differ by integer multiples of $2\pi$. A connection on a trivial bundle is **gauge trivial** when one such global map takes its normalized connection form to zero. For a closed piecewise-$C^1$ loop $\gamma$ lying in a trivialization, horizontal transport is defined by $\dot\theta=-a(\dot\gamma)$; the endpoint fibre rotation is its **holonomy**. When $a$ is one global one-form along the loop this is $\exp(-i\int_\gamma a)$. These definitions introduce no quantum state or quantum phase. The constant $\kappa_0$ is not identified with Planck's constant or a unit of electric charge.

For $b\in\mathbb R$, let $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, $r=(x^2+y^2+z^2)^{1/2}$, and define the smooth real two-form

$$
F_b:=\frac{b}{r^3}\left(x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy\right).
$$

Give $M$ its canonical Minkowski metric

$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2,$$

of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the time orientation selected by the smooth timelike vector field $N:=\partial_{x^0}$, and the product orientation $o:=dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$. Thus $(M,g,N,o)$ is the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold required by [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its underlying product smooth structure and orientation are the standard ones on this open subset of $\mathbb R^4$.

Use the standard Euclidean inner product and norm on the spatial $\mathbb R^3$ factor in all spatial dot products and radii below.

On the locus $x^2+y^2>0$, define dimensionless polar coordinates by $x=r\sin\theta\cos\phi$, $y=r\sin\theta\sin\phi$, $z=r\cos\theta$, where $0<\theta<\pi$ and $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$. There $d\phi=(x\,dy-y\,dx)/(x^2+y^2)$; only this differential, not a global real-valued angle, is used on the north-south overlap. The displayed north and south potential formulas are interpreted on angular coordinate neighborhoods and extended across their respective axes as verified in step 2.2.

In a fixed $x^0$-slice, write $S^2:=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:|u|_2=1\}$, where $|u|_2=(u_1^2+u_2^2+u_3^2)^{1/2}$, and give it the outward orientation: its area form is $\omega_u(v,w):=\det(u,v,w)$ for tangent vectors $v,w\in T_uS^2$. This is a compact smooth sphere; compactness follows from closedness and boundedness by [[thm-heine-borel-rn]].

Let $U_N=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r+z>0\}$ and $U_S=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r-z>0\}$; these two open sets cover $M$. Then $dF_b=0$ and its flux through the unit sphere with outward orientation is $4\pi b$. If $b\ne0$, $F_b$ has no global one-form potential on $M$. On $U_N$ and $U_S$,

$$
A_N=b(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad A_S=-b(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi
$$

are smooth local potentials with $dA_N=dA_S=F_b$, and $A_S-A_N=-2b\,d\phi$ on the overlap. For a chosen normalization $\kappa_0>0$, these local forms define the normalized circle-connection data of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] precisely when the transition $g_{NS}=e^{-2ib\phi/\kappa_0}$ is single-valued, equivalently $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$. For a smooth loop $g(e^{i\phi})=e^{i\chi(\phi)}$, its winding is $[\chi(2\pi)-\chi(0)]/(2\pi)$, with both circles oriented by increasing angle. Existence of a smooth phase lift, integrality of its endpoint change, and independence of the lift are proved in the phase-lift construction below. The transition winding has sign $-2b/\kappa_0$ in the stated north-to-south convention, while $\int_{S^2}F_b/(2\pi\kappa_0)=2b/\kappa_0$. This is an exact condition for this chosen circle normalization, not a claim that every classical real flux is quantized. When $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$, the compatible two-set data also produce a smooth principal circle-bundle connection, using the actual set-size interface in [A1] and the gluing statement of [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]].

There is also a flat example with nontrivial holonomy. On $M_0=\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb R^2$ with product smooth structure, take $S^1=U(1)$ with the smooth structure defined above. Write $w\in S^1$ for the base-circle coordinate and let $\nu=-i w^{-1}dw$ be its global real angular one-form, normalized by $\int_{S^1}\nu=2\pi$. For dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$, set $A=\kappa_0 a\,\nu$. On the product bundle $P_0=M_0\times U(1)$ with projection $\pi(x,z)=x$ and right action $(x,z)\cdot\zeta=(x,z\zeta)$, use $\omega=\vartheta+a\pi^*\nu$, where $z\in U(1)$ is the fibre coordinate and $\vartheta=-i z^{-1}dz$ is its real angular form. Holonomy means the fibre multiplier of the horizontal lift around the indicated base loop; gauge trivial means gauge-equivalent to $\vartheta$ under a smooth bundle map $G_u(x,z)=(x,z u(x))$ covering the identity. Then $F=dA=0$ but holonomy around the circle is $e^{-2\pi ia}$, so this connection is gauge trivial exactly when $a\in\mathbb Z$. If $b$ and $\kappa_0$ are assigned physical units, both are measured in webers; the ratio $2b/\kappa_0$ is dimensionless. No general classification of circle bundles is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

derivations.claim:
The four-chain balance in [F1] gives
$Q(\Sigma_2)-Q(\Sigma_1)=-Q(B)$. In [F1], the finite-chain functional
$Q(C)$ is defined as $c^{-1}\int_C i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ for every three-chain
$C$; thus its $Q(B)$ equals the source-current flux $\Phi_j(B)$ defined here.
This is exactly the claimed signed identity, conditional on the sourced
Maxwell equations in [A1] as in [F1].

The bounding-surface clause of [F1] gives
$\int_{\partial W}F=0$ for every finite smooth three-chain $W$. If $j=0$
throughout $W$, [A1] and [F4] give $d*F=0$ there, and finite smooth Stokes
then yields $\int_{\partial W}*F=\int_Wd*F=0$. A closed nonbounding surface
is not $\partial W$ for a chain in the field domain, so these arguments assign
it no flux value.

The draft supplier [F3] states that $F_b$ is smooth and closed on the
punctured domain. In spherical coordinates
$x=r\sin\theta\cos\phi$, $y=r\sin\theta\sin\phi$,
$z=r\cos\theta$, the form restricts to
$F_b=b\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$ on each sphere $S^2_r$, so direct integration over
$0\leq\theta\leq\pi$, $0\leq\phi\leq2\pi$ yields
$\int_{S^2_r}F_b=4\pi b\ne0$. If the sphere were the boundary of a finite
smooth three-chain in that domain, the closed-form bounding-surface result
[F1] would force this integral to vanish. Thus it is nonbounding with
nonzero magnetic flux, conditional on the exact claim of draft supplier [F3];
this use does not constitute independent proof acceptance of that supplier.

In the positively oriented orthonormal spherical coframe
$e^0=dx^0$, $e^1=dr$, $e^2=r\,d\theta$, $e^3=r\sin\theta\,d\phi$,
$F_b=(b/r^2)e^2\wedge e^3$. The Hodge formula of [F5] gives
$*F_b=(b/r^2)e^0\wedge e^1=(b/r^2)dx^0\wedge dr$ because the complementary
index permutation $(2,3,0,1)$ is even and both spatial metric signs are
positive. Hence on this dense polar-coordinate region
$d*F_b=d(b/r^2)\wedge dx^0\wedge dr=0$; smoothness of $F_b$ and $g$ extends
this identity across the polar axes. Along with $dF_b=0$ from [F3], [F4]
gives $\nabla_aF_b^{ab}=0$, so $F_b$ satisfies the smooth
source-free Maxwell equations adopted in [A1] with $j=0$.

If $\Sigma$ is a compact boundaryless finite smooth three-cycle, then
$\partial\Sigma=0$. The Gauss formula in [F1] therefore gives
$Q(\Sigma)=(\mu_0c)^{-1}\int_{\partial\Sigma}*F=0$. This is the stated
compact-slice neutrality consequence.

[A2, F2] distinguishes the global real closed-form model from an additional
normalized circle-connection choice. Thus the bounding-surface deductions
above impose neither exactness of every closed field form nor a flux rule on
nonbounding cycles, and they introduce no charge-quantization premise.

Put $\widetilde F:=-*F_b$. Then $d\widetilde F=-d*F_b=0$, and [F5]
gives $*\widetilde F=-*^2F_b=F_b$; consequently
$d*\widetilde F=dF_b=0$, so [F4] also gives the source-free divergence
equation for $\widetilde F$. Its electric flux through the same nonbounding
sphere is $\int_{S^2_r}*\widetilde F=\int_{S^2_r}F_b=4\pi b\ne0$. By [F4],
$\widetilde F$ also satisfies the adopted equations [A1] with $j=0$. These are
smooth fields on the punctured domain and make no source or field assertion at
the excluded origin.

derivations.claim:
For $\mathbf E=(E_0,0,0)$ and $\mathbf B=0$, [F1] gives
$T^{00}=\epsilon_0E_0^2/2$ and $T^{0i}=0$. The electric quadratic matrix
$E_iE_j-\delta_{ij}|E|^2/2$ is
$\operatorname{diag}(E_0^2/2,-E_0^2/2,-E_0^2/2)$, so the minus sign in the
spatial formula of [F1] gives the displayed spatial diagonal. Contracting with
$g_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ yields
$T^a{}_a=-\epsilon_0E_0^2/2-\epsilon_0E_0^2/2+\epsilon_0E_0^2/2+\epsilon_0E_0^2/2=0$.
The spatial diagonal entries are all equal exactly when
$\epsilon_0E_0^2/2=0$, equivalently $E_0=0$ since $\epsilon_0>0$.
Then all tensor components vanish; otherwise the spatial stress is
anisotropic by the definition in the Example.

For $\mathbf E=0$ and $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_0)$, [F1] gives
$T^{00}=B_0^2/(2\mu_0)$ and $T^{0i}=0$. The magnetic quadratic matrix
$B_iB_j-\delta_{ij}|B|^2/2$ is
$\operatorname{diag}(-B_0^2/2,-B_0^2/2,B_0^2/2)$, so the spatial minus
sign in [F1] gives the displayed magnetic diagonal. Its metric trace is
$-B_0^2/(2\mu_0)+B_0^2/(2\mu_0)+B_0^2/(2\mu_0)-B_0^2/(2\mu_0)=0$.
The spatial diagonal entries are all equal exactly when
$B_0^2/(2\mu_0)=0$, equivalently $B_0=0$ since $\mu_0>0$.
Then all tensor components vanish; otherwise the spatial stress is
anisotropic by the definition in the Example.
The calculation is pointwise and supplies no global or empirical claim.
